tower.rail.heading: The network
tower.signIn.companyLede: For the people who run one of the companies in this network. You will see your own company — and, if you are the group, the sisters under it.
tower.signIn.companyHint: Your account was created by whoever administers your company. Everything you change here is recorded against your name.
tower.signIn.needBoth: Both the email and the password are needed.
tower.signIn.title: Setup key
tower.signIn.lede: The one shared operator key — for creating the first staff accounts, and for scripts. It acts with full operator rights, but it cannot say who is holding it, so outside a sandbox it cannot take a decision that needs two people.
tower.signIn.staffLede: For the people who work for the network. Your name comes from your account, so every decision you make here — including the ones that need a second person — is recorded against you.
tower.signIn.staffHint: New here? Open the link in the email you were sent, and choose your password first.
tower.welcome.title: Choose your password
tower.welcome.lede: A network staff account was made for {name}. Nobody was shown a password for it: choose your own, and then sign in with this address.
tower.welcome.hint: At least 10 characters. Not your name or email address, not a common word with a number on the end, and not only digits.
tower.welcome.needTen: A password needs at least 10 characters.
tower.welcome.noMatch: The two passwords are not the same.
tower.welcome.done: Your password is set. Sign in with it now.
tower.signIn.name: Your name
tower.signIn.nameHint: Kept with every decision you make here. It is not verified — the key below is what proves you may be here, and your name is what tells the next person who made the call.
tower.signIn.keyHint: The shared operator credential. It is never stored on this machine beyond this browser tab: close the tab and this console is signed out.
tower.signIn.keySandbox: On a sandbox server with no operator key configured, any value is accepted.
tower.signIn.needName: Say who you are — every decision here is recorded against a name.
tower.signIn.ended: Your session ended. Sign in again.
tower.password.signInAgainCompany: Password changed. You were signed out here and everywhere else — sign in again with the new password.
tower.password.signInAgain: Password changed. Every staff session was signed out — sign in again with the new password.
tower.twoStep.title: Two-step sign-in
tower.twoStep.step1: Install an authenticator app on your phone — Google or Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password, or one you already use.
tower.twoStep.step2: In the app, add an account and scan this code, or type the key.
tower.twoStep.step3: Type the 6-digit code the app shows.
tower.twoStep.qrLabel: QR code for your authenticator app
tower.twoStep.keyHint: Time-based, 6 digits. Never share it: it is the second half of your sign-in.
tower.twoStep.needCode: Type the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
tower.twoStep.setupLede: Staff sign in with a password and a code from an authenticator app. You set it up once; it takes a minute.
tower.twoStep.codeLede: Open your authenticator app and type the code it shows for SeeBuyGet.
tower.twoStep.lost: Lost your phone? Two other members of staff can reset your two-step sign-in, under Network → Network staff.
tower.twoStep.onBody: You sign in with your password and a code from your authenticator app.
tower.twoStep.offBody: Your account signs in with a password only. Outside the sandbox, staff cannot sign in without two-step sign-in — set it up now and nothing changes for you at launch.
tower.twoStep.settingsLede: How you sign in to the console.
tower.twoStep.nudge: Two-step sign-in is off for your account. It is required outside the sandbox.
tower.staff.resetAsked: Reset asked by {name}. A second member of staff approves it.
tower.live.onHint: Lists and counts update by themselves as things change.
tower.live.backHint: The live connection dropped. It is trying again; until then, Refresh reads now.
tower.password.onlyCompany: The setup key has no password to change here.
tower.staff.title: Network staff
tower.staff.lede: One sign-in per person, so a decision that needs two people really takes two. That goes for a new sign-in too: one member of staff asks for it and a second approves it. The new person is emailed a link to choose their own password; nobody on staff is ever shown one.
tower.staff.ledeKey: You are signed in with the setup key. Outside a sandbox it makes a staff account alone only while nobody can sign in, approves a request only for somebody who is the only one able to sign in, and takes no sign-in away without a day’s notice to everybody on staff.
tower.setup.title: Setting up network staff
tower.setup.lede: You are signed in with the setup key. On this server it sets network staff up and does nothing else: it opens no other screen, decides nothing and acts for nobody. Make the first account here, then sign in with it.
tower.staff.asked: Asked. Nothing is made yet. When a second person approves it, {name} is emailed a link to choose a password. Nobody on staff is shown one.
tower.staff.askedKey: Asked. Nothing is made yet. You are the only one who can sign in, so you approve it yourself with the setup key: sign out, sign in with the setup key, and approve it under Network staff. Then {name} is emailed a link to choose a password. Nobody on staff is shown one.
tower.staff.waiting.title: Asked for, waiting for a second member of staff
tower.staff.waiting.mine: You asked on {when}. A second member of staff approves it. It waits until {until}.
tower.staff.waiting.mineKey: You asked on {when}. You are the only one who can sign in, so the setup key approves this one. It waits until {until}.
tower.staff.waiting.keyApproves: {who} asked on {when} and is the only one who can sign in, so the setup key is their second. Approve it only if you know this person and this is their address. It waits until {until}.
tower.staff.waiting.theirs: {who} asked on {when}. Approve it only if you know this person and this is their address. It waits until {until}.
tower.staff.waiting.key: {who} asked on {when}. A second member of staff decides, signed in with their own account. It waits until {until}.
tower.staff.invited.title: {name} can now choose a password
tower.staff.invited.sent: An email is on its way to {email} with a link to choose a password. It works once, for 48 hours. Nobody on staff is shown a password.
tower.staff.invited.notSent: The email to {email} could not be sent just now. It is tried again for a day. You can also send a new link from the list below.
tower.staff.invited.sandbox: On this laptop no email leaves. This is the link that was written:
tower.staff.noPassword: Has not chosen a password yet
tower.staff.linkUntil: The link in their email works until {when}.
tower.staff.linkLapsed: The link in their email has lapsed.
tower.staff.removalAsked: The setup key asked to take this sign-in away. It can from {when}, unless somebody on staff stops it.
tower.staff.name: Full name
tower.staff.nameHint: Recorded against every decision they make.
tower.staff.revealBody: Made with the setup key, so it has a first password. It is shown once and never again, and only to you. Whoever it is for changes it after their first sign-in.
tower.staff.none: No staff accounts yet. Everybody is signing in with the setup key, so no decision here can be told apart by person.
tower.risks.title: Risk register
tower.risks.lede: Every corridor and hub, rated low, medium or high for pilferage, hijacking, unrest and roadblock extortion, and looked at again each quarter. An incident proposes a raise; one of us decides. A HIGH rating asks for seals and no night running: on a corridor, parcels only in a bag closed on a coded seal and nothing between 19:00 and 06:00; at a hub, a bag leaves only on a coded seal and none is loaded at night.
tower.risks.proposedLede: Nothing changes until one of us decides. Keeping it as it is takes a reason, which is kept beside the incident.
tower.risks.keepWhy: Why it stays as it is
tower.risks.col.name: Name
tower.risks.whyPh: What you know: incidents, reports, the season
tower.risks.highHub: High: from now a bag leaves this hub only on a coded seal, and none is loaded here between 19:00 and 06:00. The hub is told.
tower.risks.highCorridor: High: from now parcels travel on this corridor only in a bag closed on a coded seal, and nothing goes onto it between 19:00 and 06:00. A fleet running it is told.
tower.risks.rated: Rated, and dated in your name.
tower.risks.kept: Kept as it is, with your reason.
tower.declarations.title: Security declarations
tower.declarations.lede: Every shop, hub, fleet and rider in no fleet signs a short security declaration at joining and again each year. Without one in force they take on nothing new. They sign it themselves, in their own app; nobody here signs for them.
tower.declarations.allSigned: Every partner has a security declaration in force.
tower.riderIds.title: Riders’ ID photos
tower.riderIds.lede: A bicycle or motorcycle rider in no fleet rides at once. Until one of us has seen a photo of their ID, how many parcels they may carry at once stays where their country’s cap starts. Look that it is an ID card, readable, and theirs.
tower.riderIds.none: No rider’s ID photo is waiting.
tower.riderIds.whyLabel: Why not: the rider is shown this, and sends another
tower.riderIds.seen: Seen. Their cap grows from now, and they have been told.
tower.riderIds.sentBack: Sent back. They have been told why, and send another.
tower.roles.languagesCovers: proofreading the apps’ words, for their country — nothing else
tower.countries.pickHint: They see the records and lists of these countries, and nothing of any other. You can give only countries you work in yourself.
tower.countries.changeHint: Nothing changes until a second member of staff approves. They are then signed out, and sign in again to work in the new countries. A change that only takes countries away they may approve themselves.
tower.countries.everyOption: Every country — only somebody who works in every country can give this
tower.countries.changeWaiting: A change of countries waits for a second person
tower.countries.asked: Asked: {name} works in the new countries once a second member of staff approves.
tower.countries.approved: {name} now works in the new countries, and signs in again to use them.
tower.countries.waitingTheirs: {who} asked on {when}. Approve it only if this person should work in these countries. It waits until {until}.
tower.countries.waitingAboutYou: {who} asked on {when} to add to your own countries, so somebody else decides it. It waits until {until}.
tower.countries.waitingFewer: {who} asked on {when} that you work in fewer countries. You may approve it yourself — fewer countries is never a way in. It waits until {until}.
tower.countries.pickerHint: Lists show this country only. A record of another of your countries still opens.
tower.countries.onlyHint: The country you work in: you see its records and lists, and nothing of any other.
tower.roles.pickHint: Each role opens only its own screens. Pick at least one: a second member of staff approves the roles with the account.
tower.roles.changeHint: Pick at least one. Nothing changes until a second member of staff approves; then this person is signed out, and signs in again to work with the new roles.
tower.roles.keyMakesAll: The setup key’s first account holds every role, because that person sets the network up. Every account asked for after it says its roles.
tower.roles.changeWaiting: A change of roles is waiting for a second member of staff.
tower.roles.asked: Asked. {name}’s roles change once a second member of staff approves. Until then nothing changes.
tower.roles.approved: {name} now holds the new roles. They were signed out, and sign in again to work with them.
tower.roles.waitingTheirs: {who} asked on {when}. Approve it only if this person should hold these roles. It waits until {until}.
tower.roles.waitingAboutYou: {who} asked on {when} to change your own roles, so somebody else decides it. It waits until {until}.
tower.roles.notYours: This screen is for another role. An administrator can give you that role, and a second one approves it.
tower.outdated.title: This console is out of date
tower.outdated.body: The server is running a newer version. Reload the page to pick it up.
tower.hazards.title: Road hazards waiting on you
tower.hazards.lede: Drivers report what is on the road, and a driver saying a hazard is gone does not remove it. Clearing one is the only way it stops warning, and only from here. A border reported closed waits here whether or not anyone disputes it, because what the network does about it is a staff decision.
tower.hazards.caveatLead: Everything in this list is still warning every driver
tower.hazards.caveat: — at full weight, and still blocking the same loads. A dispute changes nothing on its own, and that is deliberate: being wrong about a bridge that is not there costs a detour, being wrong about one that is still there kills somebody.
tower.hazards.borderAdmin: Switching a crossing off is for staff who hold the administration role.
tower.hazards.emptyBody: No driver is currently saying a reported hazard has gone, and no border is reported closed. That is not the same as the map being up to date — it only means nobody has said otherwise.
tower.hazards.evidence: {confirmations} saw it · {refutations} say it is gone
tower.hazards.photoNone: No photograph with this one. That is not a reason to discount it — a driver who could not safely stop still reported what they saw.
tower.hazards.noAccounts: This hazard was reported before accounts were kept, so all there is to go on is the note and the counts above. Ring the fleet before clearing it.
tower.hazards.clearTitle: Take this off every driver’s map
tower.hazards.clearBody: It stops warning immediately, everywhere. The record is kept with your name and your reason, so the decision can be reviewed — and a driver who meets it again can report it afresh.
tower.hazards.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. Council confirmed the bridge was rebuilt to 6.0 m on 4 September
tower.hazards.reasonHint: Kept forever, and read by whoever asks later why this hazard vanished.
tower.hazards.cleared: Cleared {hazard} — the reason is on the record.
tower.papers.title: Papers: couriers and vehicles without a fleet
tower.papers.lede: A fleet records its own vehicles’ and drivers’ renewals in the Fleet app. A courier who rides without a fleet, and a vehicle no fleet owns, have no office to do that — a licence that lapses puts them off the road with nobody to tell. Record what you have seen here; the new date is the whole of the renewal.
tower.anchors.title: The trail, anchored outside our database
tower.anchors.lede: Every pickup, delivery, seal, scan and damage report is fingerprinted into one chain. Once a day its newest link goes to an auditor’s address, where we cannot change it. If anything up to that link is changed later, the chain no longer gives the same link, and the auditor’s copy shows it.
tower.anchors.notMatching: {n, plural, one {# day no longer matches} other {# days no longer match}}
tower.anchors.notDelivered: No mail provider is wired yet: each day is kept here, and the email waits in the outbox until one is.
tower.anchors.noAuditor: Nobody named yet: each day is kept here only
tower.anchors.waiting: {by} asked for {address} on {date}. It counts once a second member of staff approves.
tower.anchors.waitingMine: You asked for {address} on {date}. It counts once another member of staff approves.
tower.anchors.declineWhy: Why not — the person who asked reads this
tower.anchors.twoPeople: Two people: you ask, another member of staff approves. The address it had is told.
tower.anchors.noDays: Nothing kept yet: the first goes a few minutes after midnight UTC.
tower.anchors.checkLede: Type the link number and the fingerprint from one of the auditor’s emails: the chain says whether it still gives that fingerprint there.
tower.shopLicences.title: Shops’ trading licences
tower.shopLicences.lede: Staff note the date a shop’s licence runs to when it is approved, and again at each renewal. The shop is told thirty days before; fourteen days after it lapses, no new parcel can start there until the renewed one is recorded. Booked parcels and its shelf go on.
tower.shopLicences.waiting: {n, plural, one {# licence sent} other {# licences sent}}
tower.shopLicences.allInDate: Every shop’s licence is in date ({n, plural, one {# shop} other {# shops}}).
tower.shopLicences.inDateCount: And {n, plural, one {# shop} other {# shops}} in date.
tower.shopLicences.noDateRow: Approved before its date was asked — note it from the licence on record
tower.shopLicences.sentRead: Sent {date}. The shop reads it as valid until {expires}.
tower.shopLicences.photoOnRecord: The licence this date is read from
tower.shopLicences.noPhoto: No photograph of this licence is stored.
tower.shopLicences.lastRefused: The last licence it sent was not accepted: “{reason}” — {who}, {date}.
tower.shopLicences.nothingSent: Nothing is waiting: the shop sends its renewed licence from the Shop app’s home screen.
tower.shopLicences.dateIt: Note the date, from the licence on record
tower.shopLicences.readDate: Valid until, as you read it on the licence
tower.shopLicences.dateFromRecord: Valid until, as you read it on the licence on record
tower.shopLicences.differs: The shop read {expires}. Look again before saving: two readings of one licence disagree.
tower.shopLicences.refuseWhy: Why not — the shop is shown exactly this
tower.shopLicences.refuseSend: Send it back and tell them
tower.shopLicences.refusedDone: {name} is told its licence was not accepted.
tower.observations.title: What people were asked for at the border
tower.observations.lede: First-hand accounts from drivers and agents at a counter: which paper, where, on which day. The rules above are ours to keep; these are somebody’s afternoon, and they are shown as that.
tower.observations.basis: Not what any border requires. A requirement that ended shows here as nobody having been asked since — nothing is ever marked stale by hand.
tower.observations.none: Nobody has recorded anything here yet.
tower.observations.consent: {who} agreed on {when} that the numbers were blacked out (notice v{version})
tower.observations.removeKeeps: The observation stays — it was first-hand and still is. Only the picture goes, and your reason is kept beside it.
tower.observations.removed: Removed. The observation is still there, now without its photograph.
tower.papers.transitLede: A container cleared inland travels from the quay under bond, and only a carrier holding a transit authority in that country is offered the load. A fleet keeps its own driving licences in the fleet app; this one has no office but ours, and when it lapses the carrier simply stops being offered bonded work.
tower.papers.transitBasis: Recorded as the carrier states it, against whoever typed it. We check that one exists and is in date; we do not verify it with the authority that issued it.
tower.papers.transitNone: Nobody is recorded as able to carry uncleared goods.
tower.papers.transitDays: {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} left
tower.papers.transitLapsed: lapsed {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago
tower.papers.transitWithdrawn: Withdrawn. It stays on the record.
tower.papers.sweepLast: Last ran {time}: ended {shifts, plural, one {# shift} other {# shifts}} on lapsed papers, sent {told, plural, one {# notice} other {# notices}} to drivers, fleets and shops, sent {mails, plural, one {# fleet email} other {# fleet emails}}. It runs every {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}.
tower.papers.sweepNever: Has not run since this server started. It runs every {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}, and can be run now.
tower.papers.sweepDone: The check ran: {shifts, plural, one {# shift} other {# shifts}} ended, {told, plural, one {# driver} other {# drivers}} told, {mails, plural, one {# fleet email} other {# fleet emails}} sent.
tower.papers.fleetsLine: The fleets look after their own: {count, plural, one {# active fleet} other {# active fleets}}, {withLapsed} with a lapsed paper right now ({lapsed} lapsed, {due} running out) — each sees it on its own dashboard and gets the email.

tower.papers.noCouriersTitle: No courier rides without a fleet
tower.papers.noCouriersBody: Everyone who drives is in a fleet, and that fleet’s office records their papers.
tower.papers.vehiclesTitle: Vehicles no fleet owns · {n} ({stuck} off the road)
tower.papers.noVehiclesBody: Every registered vehicle belongs to a fleet, whose office records its papers.
